It is the smallest context that would contain both statements. No delivered statement relates its radius part to its ladder part, so it is a candidate context, not a shared context: the Goldschmidt authority has no ladder term and the KashaVavilov authority has no radius term.

GdSvCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii with the band edges (lo, hi) and the Stern-Volmer measured slope pair (slopeI, slopeTau) of the intensity and lifetime responses. A verdict equivalence would have to live here. The radius triple fixes a lattice contact ratio; the slope pair is a concentration-response datum with no ionic-radius component, and no delivered statement maps one part onto the other.

GdQyCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii with band edges plus a finite vector of channel rates k. The Goldschmidt side decides a band membership on a length ratio; the QuantumYield side decides the share of one channel in the total rate. A shared context would need a delivered statement identifying a radius ratio with a rate share, and none exists.

GdFpCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii with band edges plus the five FluorPhos channel rates. Both endpoints are three-way classifiers, so the candidate context is the only place a verdict equivalence could live; but the decision functions read a single real radius ratio on one side and two rational products on the other, and no delivered statement maps the two input families.

GdEgCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii plus the energy-gap-law reorganization energy and gap coordinate (lam, x). The Goldschmidt statements read lengths only; lam and x are energies, and the only delivered occurrence of a Marcus barrier in the corpus is the Kernel copy that EnergyGapLaw pins. No delivered statement sends a radius to an energy.

GdSsCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii plus the StokesShift surfaces (lam, e00). The Stokes statements are differences of electronic energies on two harmonic surfaces; the Goldschmidt statements are ratios of ionic contact lengths. The context is a union of two vocabularies, not a shared observable.

GdIcCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii plus an IC barrier coordinate (lamI, xI) and a spin-orbit coupling HSO. The ICvsISC statement orders two Franck-Condon barriers; the Goldschmidt statement orders a radius ratio against a band. No delivered statement carries a spin-orbit coupling into the lattice vocabulary or a radius into the rate vocabulary.

GdFrCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii plus a Forster radius and a donor-acceptor separation (R0, R). Both endpoints are geometric threshold criteria, which is why the legacy register calls the pair a look-alike. The lengths are nevertheless different objects: R is an intermolecular separation in solution, R0 is a spectroscopic length built from the overlap integral and the orientation factor, and rA/rB/rO are ionic contact radii in a crystal. No delivered statement maps one family onto the other.

GdEiCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the perovskite radii plus an Einstein A coefficient. The shared symbol tau is the only link the names offer: on the Goldschmidt side tauGoldschmidt is the dimensionless 3/20 of the radius rule, on the Einstein side tauR is the radiative lifetime 1/A. A lifetime is not a radius tolerance, and no delivered statement maps a radius to a rate.

queries.title: Is the tolerance-factor band verdict a property of the Kasha-Vavilov ladder?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Does the Goldschmidt band verdict `GoldschmidtConforms lo hi rA rB rO` - a statement about the A-O contact distance in a cubic ABO3 perovskite - constrain the lossless Kasha/Vavilov separation `lossless_separates_kasha_vavilov`, whose witness is a ladder of radiative and internal-conversion rates?
queries.chemicalRationale: Goldschmidt measures a ratio of ionic contact lengths, t = (rA + rO) / (sqrt 2 * (rB + rO)), and the band verdict tests that ratio against edges (lo, hi). The Kasha-Vavilov statement is a separation theorem about a ladder of per-level radiative rates rad n and internal-conversion rates ic n; its witness is rad = 1 with ic 0 = 0, where Kasha holds and Vavilov fails. A relation would need a shared quantity: an excited-state branching fraction on one side and a lattice length ratio on the other. Neither statement measures the other's quantity. The only similarity is that both decide a two-way split (in-band/out-of-band versus Kasha/Vavilov), which is a statement shape, not a shared observable.

queries.title: Do the Goldschmidt zone classifier and the Stern-Volmer zone classifier decide the same classification?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Does the three-way Goldschmidt classifier `goldschmidtZone lo hi t`, which compares one real tolerance factor against a band, coincide with the four-way Stern-Volmer classifier `svZoneQ slopeI slopeTau`, which reads a pair of rational slopes?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both endpoints are data classifiers of a measured scalar against a band, so a verdict equivalence is the natural query. Goldschmidt classifies the radius ratio t into tooSmall/ideal/tooLarge by testing t < lo and then t <= hi. Stern-Volmer classifies a measured slope pair into dynLike/statLike/mixedLike/inconsistent by comparing slopeI and slopeTau; it has four verdicts, not three, and its input is a pair of rational concentration-response slopes, not one real length ratio. A verdict equivalence would need a total translation from (slopeI, slopeTau) to (lo, hi, t) that preserves the decision boundaries. No delivered statement provides one, and the translation would have to identify a photophysical response slope with a lattice length ratio.

queries.title: Is the in-band predicate on the tolerance factor a quantum-yield statement?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the band membership `InBand lo hi t` on the tolerance factor the same kind of statement as the channel yield `yieldOf k i`, the share of channel i in the total rate?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both endpoints are ratios with a "part of a whole" reading: `InBand` tests a length ratio against two edges, and `yieldOf k i = k i / totalRate k` is the share of one decay channel in the total decay. The similarity is arithmetic, not physical. A quantum yield is an excited-state branching probability that sums to one over the channels; a band membership is a geometric packing verdict with no normalisation. Goldschmidt has no rate parameter and QuantumYield has no radius or length; the candidate bridge would have to read a radius ratio as a rate share.

queries.title: Does the Goldschmidt zone verdict coincide with the FluorPhos competition verdict?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Does the Goldschmidt band classifier `goldschmidtZone lo hi t` coincide with the FluorPhos competition classifier `fpZoneQ kF kISC kIC kP kNR`, which decides between fluorescence-dominant, balanced and phosphorescence-dominant decay?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both endpoints are three-way classifiers, so a verdict correspondence is the natural query. The decision functions differ: Goldschmidt tests one real t against (lo, hi), while FluorPhos compares kISC * kP with kF * (kP + kNR) over the rationals. The FluorPhos classifier takes five channel rates as arguments, and its own docstring and the build linter record that kIC is not consumed by the decision body, so even the partner classifier does not decide an internal-conversion rate. A verdict correspondence would need a translation from the five rates to (lo, hi, t); none is delivered, and it would have to read a competition between radiative and intersystem-crossing channels as a lattice contact ratio.

queries.title: Is the A-O rattling gap the nonradiative barrier?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the Goldschmidt A-O rattling gap `gapA rA rB rO`, a signed length, the same object as the energy-gap-law nonradiative barrier `nrBarrier lam x`, an energy?
queries.chemicalRationale: The names invite the identification: one is a "gap" and the other a "barrier". The objects do not match. `gapA rA rB rO = idealAO rB rO - (rA + rO)` is a length in angstrom, linear in the radii and antisymmetric under exchanging the actual and ideal A-O contact. `nrBarrier lam x = (lam - x)^2 / (4 lam)` is an energy, quadratic in (lam - x) and singular at lam = 0. Their dimensions, their dependence on their arguments and their physical readings all differ; the only overlap is the English word "gap". No delivered statement maps a radius triple to (lam, x).

queries.title: Is the Goldschmidt lattice parameter the Forster radius?

queries.title: Is Goldschmidt tau the Einstein radiative lifetime?
